topo-01-c1.text: (2011). Maths in a minute: The fundamental group. Plus Magazine, University of Cambridge.
topo-01-c1.quote: In the field of topology two shapes are considered the same if one can be deformed into the other without tearing or cutting.
topo-01-c1.claim: You can stretch it, bend it and squish it, but you can't tear it or glue pieces together.

topo-01-c2.text: John M. Lee (2012). Simply Connected Spaces. Georgia Institute of Technology, School of Mathematics (course handout).
topo-01-c2.quote: The surface of a doughnut is topologically equivalent (or homeomorphic) to the surface of a coﬀee cup with one handle, but not to a sphere. This example is used to illustrate that homeomorphisms can bend, stretch, and shrink but not tear or collapse.
topo-01-c2.claim: Two shapes are homeomorphic (topologically equivalent) if one can be continuously deformed into the other.

topo-02-c1.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. Felix Klein - Biography. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
topo-02-c1.quote: A Klein bottle cannot be constructed in Euclidean space. It is best pictured as a cylinder looped back through itself to join with its other end.

topo-02-c2.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. A history of Topology. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
topo-02-c2.quote: Möbius published a description of a Möbius band in 1865. He tried to describe the 'one-sided' property of the Möbius band in terms of non-orientability.
topo-02-c2.claim: The strip has only one side!

topo-02-c3.text: Abigail Kirk (2007). Euler's polyhedron formula. Plus Magazine, University of Cambridge.
topo-02-c3.quote: In the 19th century mathematicians discovered that all surfaces in three-dimensional space are essentially characterised by the number of holes they have: our simple polyhedra have no holes, a doughnut has one hole, etc.
topo-02-c3.claim: The Classification Theorem says every closed orientable surface is determined by its genus.

topo-03-c1.text: Abigail Kirk (2007). Euler's polyhedron formula. Plus Magazine, University of Cambridge.
topo-03-c1.quote: So, V - E + F = 8 - 12 + 6 = 14 - 12 = 2 which is what Euler's formula tells us it should be.

topo-03-c2.text: Abigail Kirk (2007). Euler's polyhedron formula. Plus Magazine, University of Cambridge.
topo-03-c2.quote: For any polyhedron, V - E + F is exactly 2 minus 2 times the number of holes! It turns out that this number, called the Euler characteristic, is crucial to the study of all three-dimensional surfaces, not just polyhedra.
topo-03-c2.claim: For a surface of genus g (with g holes): χ = 2 - 2g

topo-03-c3.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. A history of Topology. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
topo-03-c3.quote: This was the first known result on a topological invariant.
topo-03-c3.claim: The Euler characteristic is a topological invariant: it doesn't change when you deform the surface.

topo-04-c2.text: Knots (math circle notes). University of Utah, Department of Mathematics.
topo-04-c2.quote: There is a famous theorem proved by the German mathematician Kurt Reidemeister in 1920’s that says: If two knot diagrams represent the same knot (or a link) then one can be transformed to the other by a sequence of Reidemeister moves.
topo-04-c2.claim: Two knot diagrams represent the same knot if you can get from one to the other using three types of moves

topo-04-c3.text: Knots (math circle notes). University of Utah, Department of Mathematics.
topo-04-c3.quote: A knot (or a link) is tricolorable if each strand can be colored in one of three colors with the following rules:
topo-04-c3.claim: Tricolorability: Can you color the strands with 3 colors following certain rules?

topo-05-c1.text: (2011). Maths in a minute: The fundamental group. Plus Magazine, University of Cambridge.
topo-05-c1.quote: You consider two loops to be equivalent if you can morph one into the other without cutting either of them.
topo-05-c1.claim: Two loops are considered "the same" if one can be continuously deformed into the other (this is called homotopy).

topo-05-c3.text: John M. Lee (2012). Simply Connected Spaces. Georgia Institute of Technology, School of Mathematics (course handout).
topo-05-c3.quote: Roughly speaking, we will detect “holes” by wrapping “strings” around them: a simply connected space is one in which any loop of string can be continuously shrunk to a point while remaining in the space.
topo-05-c3.claim: A space is simply connected if every loop can be shrunk to a point

topo-05-c3.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. Grigori Yakovlevich Perelman - Biography. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
topo-05-c3.quote: Can every simply connected 3-manifold be deformed into the 3-sphere? The Poincaré Conjecture asserts that the answer to this question is yes.
topo-05-c3.claim: The famous Poincaré Conjecture (proved by Perelman in 2003) states: the only simply connected, closed 3-manifold is the 3-sphere.

topo-05-c3.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. Grigori Yakovlevich Perelman - Biography. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
topo-05-c3.quote: In March 2010 the Clay Mathematics Institute announced that Perelman had met the conditions for the award of one million US dollars which they had offered for the solution of the Poincaré Conjecture.
topo-05-c3.claim: This was one of the Millennium Prize Problems!

topo-06-c1.text: Romyar Sharifi. Point-Set Topology, Chapter 3: Connected and compact spaces. UCLA, Department of Mathematics (lecture notes).
topo-06-c1.quote: A topological space X is compact if every open cover of X has a finite subcover.
topo-06-c1.claim: Formal definition: a space is compact if every open cover has a finite subcover.

topo-06-c2.text: J J O'Connor, E F Robertson. Eduard Heine - Biography. MacTutor History of Mathematics, University of St Andrews.
topo-06-c2.quote: He is best remembered for the Heine-Borel theorem:- ... a subset of the reals is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded .
topo-06-c2.claim: Heine-Borel: A subset of ℝⁿ is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded.

topo-06-c3.text: Eugene Boman, Robert Rogers (2018). 7.3: The Bolzano-Weierstrass Theorem. Mathematics LibreTexts: Real Analysis (Boman and Rogers).
topo-06-c3.quote: The proof of Extreme Value (which says that any continuous function f defined on a closed interval [a,b] must have a maximum and a minimum) takes a bit more work.
topo-06-c3.claim: Extreme Value Theorem: A continuous function on a compact set achieves its maximum and minimum.

topo-07-c1.text: Romyar Sharifi. Point-Set Topology, Chapter 3: Connected and compact spaces. UCLA, Department of Mathematics (lecture notes).
topo-07-c1.quote: A topological space X is connected if it is not a disjoint union of any two nonempty open subspaces.
topo-07-c1.claim: A space is connected if it cannot be split into two disjoint non-empty open sets.

topo-07-c2.text: Romyar Sharifi. Point-Set Topology, Chapter 3: Connected and compact spaces. UCLA, Department of Mathematics (lecture notes).
topo-07-c2.quote: Every path connected space is connected.

topo-07-c3.text: Romyar Sharifi. Point-Set Topology, Chapter 3: Connected and compact spaces. UCLA, Department of Mathematics (lecture notes).
topo-07-c3.quote: The image of a connected space under a continuous map is connected.
topo-07-c3.claim: This holds because [a,b] is connected, so f([a,b]) must be connected (continuous images of connected sets are connected).

topo-08-c1.text: Allen Hatcher (2002). Algebraic Topology. Cornell University, Department of Mathematics.
topo-08-c1.quote: However, the higher-dimensional homotopy groups have the serious drawback that they are extremely difficult to compute in general.
topo-08-c1.claim: Higher homotopy groups π₃, π₄, ... are notoriously hard to compute.

topo-08-c2.text: Allen Hatcher (2002). Algebraic Topology. Cornell University, Department of Mathematics.
topo-08-c2.quote: Fortunately there is a more computable alternative to homotopy groups: the homology groups Hn (X) .
topo-08-c2.claim: Homology groups H₀, H₁, H₂, ... provide a more computable way to count holes of each dimension.

topo-09-c2.text: Allen Hatcher (2002). Algebraic Topology. Cornell University, Department of Mathematics.
topo-09-c2.quote: This covering space is called the universal cover of X because, as our general theory will show, it is a covering space of every other connected covering space of X .
topo-09-c2.claim: It's "universal" because it covers every other covering space of X: it's the largest possible unfolding.

topo-09-c3.text: Allen Hatcher (2002). Algebraic Topology. Cornell University, Department of Mathematics.
topo-09-c3.quote: This is exemplified in one of the main results in this section, an exact correspondence between connected covering spaces of a given space X and subgroups of π1 (X) .
topo-09-c3.claim: In algebraic topology, there is a bijective correspondence between covering spaces of X (up to isomorphism) and subgroups of pi_1(X) (up to conjugacy).

topo-10-c1.text: Allen Hatcher (2002). Algebraic Topology. Cornell University, Department of Mathematics.
topo-10-c1.quote: A space X constructed in this way is called a cell complex or CW complex.
topo-10-c1.claim: A CW complex is a space built by gluing cells of increasing dimension

topo-10-c3.text: Allen Hatcher (2002). Algebraic Topology. Cornell University, Department of Mathematics.
topo-10-c3.quote: Cellular homology is a very efficient tool for computing the homology groups of CW complexes, based on degree calculations.
topo-10-c3.claim: Cellular homology computes homology groups directly from the CW structure, making calculations much simpler than the general definition.

topo-11-c1.text: Allen Hatcher (2002). Algebraic Topology. Cornell University, Department of Mathematics.
topo-11-c1.quote: Cohomology is an algebraic variant of homology, the result of a simple dualization in the definition.
topo-11-c1.claim: Cohomology is the algebraic dual of homology.

topo-11-c2.text: Allen Hatcher (2002). Algebraic Topology. Cornell University, Department of Mathematics.
topo-11-c2.quote: What is a little surprising is that contravariance leads to extra structure in cohomology. This first appears in a natural product, called cup product, which makes the cohomology groups of a space into a ring.
topo-11-c2.claim: Cohomology has an advantage over homology: the cup product gives it a ring structure.

topo-12-c1.text: Vitali Kapovitch (2014). MAT 1300, Lecture 1: Smooth manifolds. University of Toronto, Department of Mathematics.
topo-12-c1.quote: Informally a smooth manifold is a space which locally looks like an open subset of Rn .
topo-12-c1.claim: A smooth manifold is a space that locally looks like R^n, with smooth transition maps between local coordinate systems.

topo-12-c3.text: Joel Feldman, Andrew Rechnitzer, Elyse Yeager. Section 4.7: A Generalized Stokes' Theorem (optional). CLP-4 Vector Calculus (University of British Columbia), University of Kentucky mirror.
topo-12-c3.quote: As we have seen, the fundamental theorem of calculus, the divergence theorem, Greens’ theorem and Stokes’ theorem share a number of common features. There is in fact a single framework which encompasses and generalizes all of them, and there is a single theorem of which they are all special cases.
topo-12-c3.claim: This single equation unifies all of classical vector calculus
